content.text:
Run `wrangler versions upload --latest`. In wrangler 4.148.0, which this project has installed, `--latest` is one of the arguments `deploy` and `versions upload` share (`sharedDeployVersionsArgs` in `node_modules/wrangler/wrangler-dist/cli.js:235316`). It uses the newest compatibility date that your installed Wrangler supports, not today's date. So the date only moves forward when you upgrade Wrangler.

Wrangler prints a warning when you use it, telling you to set a fixed `compatibility_date` or pass `--compatibility-date` instead. I'd keep `--latest` for experiments and pin a date for production, so a Wrangler upgrade can't change runtime behavior without you noticing. One example of such a change: from compatibility date 2026-08-04, `nodejs_compat` is on by default.
